chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nadri, who said:

I said to Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام: We prayed Maghrib, and the Imam erred, so he gave salām after two rakʿahs, and we repeated the prayer. He said: Why did you repeat it? Did not the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم conclude after two rakʿahs and then complete it with two rakʿahs? Why did you not complete it?

So there is nothing in these two reports that conflicts with what we stated earlier, because the inadvertence here occurred only in that he gave salām in the second rakʿah, and the inadvertence did not occur in the number of the prayer. Whoever forgetfully gives salām in the first two rakʿahs is not required to repeat the prayer; rather, he is required to make it up with one rakʿah, according to what the two reports contain. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is...

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs after which the mistaken salām occurred
key_terms.السَّهْوَ: forgetfulness or inadvertent error during the prayer
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repeating the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ: the two narrations being cited as evidence
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib prayer, the sunset salat
key_terms.جُبْرَانُهَا: making up or compensating for the deficiency in the prayer
key_terms.فَسَلَّمَ: he gave salām, ending the prayer formally

ai.seo_question: If the Imam mistakenly ends Maghrib prayer after two rakʿahs, should the prayer be repeated or completed?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on forgetfulness in Salat al-Maghrib when the Imam gives salām after two rakʿahs. It indicates that the prayer is not to be repeated; rather, it is completed to make up the deficiency. The passage also explains that this case concerns an erroneous salām, not a mistake in the actual counted number of the prayer.
